question: Let \(x\) be chosen at random from the interval \((0, 1).\) What is the probability that \[\lfloor \log_{10} 4x \rfloor - \lfloor \log_{10} x \rfloor = 0?\] Here \(\lfloor x \rfloor\) denotes the greatest integer that is less than or equal to \(x.\)
solution:
Interpret the random choice as uniform in \(x\), so the probability is the favorable length divided by the total length \(1\). The floor of a base-ten logarithm tells us between which consecutive powers of ten its input lies.

For each integer \(k\ge1\), consider
\[
10^{-k}\le x<10^{1-k}.
\]
These disjoint intervals cover \((0,1)\), and throughout this interval \(\lfloor\log_{10}x\rfloor=-k\). The two floors are equal exactly when
\[
10^{-k}\le4x<10^{1-k}.
\]
The lower bound is automatic because \(x\ge10^{-k}\). The upper bound gives \(x<\frac52\,10^{-k}\). Thus the favorable portion of this decade is
\[
\left[10^{-k},\frac52\,10^{-k}\right),
\]
whose length is \(\frac32\,10^{-k}\).

Every favorable point belongs to exactly one decade, so we add these lengths. They form a geometric series with first term \(\frac3{20}\) and ratio \(\frac1{10}\). Since the ratio has absolute value less than \(1\),
\[
P=\frac{3/20}{1-1/10}=\frac16.
\]
The indicated endpoint inclusions describe the event exactly and do not affect its length. The answer is \(\boxed{\frac16}\), choice C.

solutionMethods.explanation:
Assume the choice is uniform in \(x\), and let \(L\) be the total favorable length in \((0,1)\). We can find \(L\) by separating the first decimal decade from the smaller, scaled copy of the whole interval.

On \([1/10,1)\), we have \(\lfloor\log_{10}x\rfloor=-1\). Equality of the floors therefore requires \(1/10\le4x<1\), so the favorable part is \([1/10,1/4)\). Its length is
\[
\frac14-\frac1{10}=\frac3{20}.
\]
For \(0<x<1/10\), put \(u=10x\), so \(0<u<1\). Then
\[
\log_{10}x=\log_{10}u-1,
\qquad
\log_{10}(4x)=\log_{10}(4u)-1.
\]
Subtracting an integer from a number subtracts that same integer from its floor. Hence the difference of the two floors is unchanged: \(x\) is favorable exactly when \(u\) is favorable. Scaling back from \(u\) to \(x=u/10\) divides every length by \(10\), so the favorable length below \(1/10\) is \(L/10\).

The two parts are disjoint and cover the interval, giving
\[
L=\frac3{20}+\frac L{10},
\qquad
L=\frac{3/20}{9/10}=\frac16.
\]
Since the total sampling length is \(1\), the probability is \(\boxed{\frac16}\), choice C.
